---
title: "Can reducing stagger or vertical gap restore box-wing trim without moving the CG?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 200.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 179.0      # s the probe actually used

res = box_wing_stagger_gap_trade(airplane)

min_sm_gap = float(min(r["sm_mac"] for r in res["gap_res"]) * 100.0)
gap_np_shift = float(max(r["x_np"] for r in res["gap_res"]) - min(r["x_np"] for r in res["gap_res"]))
stagger_crit = 0.40
dcm_crit = float(next(r["dcm_dde"] for r in res["stagger_res"] if abs(r["stagger"] - stagger_crit) < 1e-3))
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"+{min_sm_gap:.0f}% MAC"`]{.hero-value}
[minimum static margin achievable by reducing vertical gap without moving CG]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** No. Reducing vertical gap to [`{python} f"{res['gaps'].min():.1f} m"`]{.key} shifts the neutral point forward by only [`{python} f"{gap_np_shift:.2f} m"`]{.key}, leaving static margin hyper-stable at [`{python} f"+{min_sm_gap:.0f}% MAC"`]{.key}. Reducing stagger shrinks both untrimmed pitch moment and elevator authority proportionally to the aft wing moment arm. Below [`{python} f"{stagger_crit:.1f} m"`]{.key} stagger, elevator effectiveness [`{python} f"{dcm_crit:.4f} /°"`]{.key} collapses, preventing workable trim (@fig-box-wing-stagger-gap). Hyper-stability is not intrinsic to joined wings, but stems from imposing a staggered layout on a monoplane CG; moving the CG aft remains necessary as shown in [prior stability analysis](2026-09-30-02-what-are-the-box-wing-neutral-point-static-margin-and-elevator-require.qmd).

```{python}
#| label: fig-box-wing-stagger-gap
#| fig-cap: "Effect of longitudinal stagger and vertical gap on box-wing static margin, aft-wing elevator control authority, and trim deflection at baseline center of gravity."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.2))

# Left plot: Stagger trade
s_vals = np.array([r["stagger"] for r in res["stagger_res"]])
sm_vals = np.array([r["sm_mac"] * 100.0 for r in res["stagger_res"]])
dcm_vals = np.array([r["dcm_dde"] for r in res["stagger_res"]])
de_vals = np.array([r["de_trim"] for r in res["stagger_res"]])

ax1_twin = ax1.twinx()
p1 = ax1.plot(s_vals, sm_vals, "tab:blue", marker="o", label="Static margin [% MAC]")
p2 = ax1_twin.plot(s_vals, dcm_vals, "tab:red", marker="s", label=r"Elevator effectiveness $dC_m/d\delta_e$")

ax1.axhline(10.0, color="gray", linestyle=":", alpha=0.6, label="Nominal SM (10% MAC)")
ax1_twin.axhline(0.0, color="tab:red", linestyle="--", alpha=0.4)
ax1.set_xlabel("Longitudinal stagger [m]")
ax1.set_ylabel("Static margin [% MAC]", color="tab:blue")
ax1_twin.set_ylabel(r"Elevator authority $dC_m/d\delta_e$ [/deg]", color="tab:red")
ax1.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="tab:blue")
ax1_twin.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="tab:red")
ax1.set_title("Stagger Trade: Stability vs Control Arm")
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

lines = p1 + p2
labels = [l.get_label() for l in lines]
ax1.legend(lines, labels, loc="center left", fontsize=8)

# Right plot: Vertical gap effect
h_vals = np.array([r["h_box"] for r in res["gap_res"]])
sm_gap_vals = np.array([r["sm_mac"] * 100.0 for r in res["gap_res"]])
xnp_gap_vals = np.array([r["x_np"] for r in res["gap_res"]])

ax2_twin = ax2.twinx()
p3 = ax2.plot(h_vals, sm_gap_vals, "tab:purple", marker="^", label="Static margin [% MAC]")
p4 = ax2_twin.plot(h_vals, xnp_gap_vals, "tab:green", marker="d", label="Neutral point $x_{np}$ [m]")

ax2.set_xlabel("Vertical gap $h_{box}$ [m]")
ax2.set_ylabel("Static margin [% MAC]", color="tab:purple")
ax2_twin.set_ylabel("Neutral point position [m]", color="tab:green")
ax2.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="tab:purple")
ax2_twin.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="tab:green")
ax2.set_title("Vertical Gap Effect (s = 3.70 m)")
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

lines2 = p3 + p4
labels2 = [l.get_label() for l in lines2]
ax2.legend(lines2, labels2, loc="lower right", fontsize=8)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
